implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Buster selects and executes deterministic suites, supervises optional agent judgment, records evidence, and classifies assertion versus infrastructure failures.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 test stage executes bounded command suites through command.execute, combines their real results with supplied specialized-suite evidence, and accepts only a terminal identity-bound runtime verdict with transcript evidence.
implementationDecision.rationale: Suite policy stays in the test package while subprocesses and agent sessions remain replaceable capabilities.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Replaces the monolithic worker with one explicit execute-collect-judge reducer.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Nova consumes Buster evidence and distinguishes actionable test failure from contract, configuration, infrastructure, rate-limit, and timeout failure.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 quality gate retains the full closed failure-class matrix and maps it to pass, request-fix, or blocked outcomes.
implementationDecision.rationale: Evidence production and quality adjudication remain separate owners.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: A strict verdict reducer replaces distributed worker/gate conditionals.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Buster runs real suites, captures their output, supervises test judgment, and emits an identity-bound terminal verdict and evidence.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 package runs real bounded command suites, passes normalized evidence to runtime.dispatch, validates terminal session/transcript evidence, and writes a durable verdict artifact.
implementationDecision.rationale: This restores execution behavior without embedding subprocess or session authority in the stage.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: One small state flow replaces the worker's scheduler, polling, and process internals.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: The quality gate evaluates Buster evidence across every supported failure class and chooses pass, remediation, or terminal block.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 package keeps the complete failure-class matrix in one strict decoder and returns only typed core-owned control results.
implementationDecision.rationale: Nova must adjudicate Buster evidence so Buster cannot approve itself.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Centralizes verdict contradictions and removes worker scheduling from the gate.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Forge reads bounded repository text while rejecting missing, non-file, oversized, traversal, and symlink-escape paths.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 repository adapter preserves those read-only outcomes behind one narrowly granted capability.
implementationDecision.rationale: The direct read-only adapter is already the smallest safe boundary.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Removes all Git mutation and agent lifecycle authority from repository reads.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Forge starts and monitors implementation sessions, verifies identity and completion, captures handoff and transcript evidence, terminates sessions, and classifies retryable versus terminal failures.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The implementation stage requires a closed runtime-owned session record with identity, timestamps, transcript digest, handoffs, termination, changed paths, and checks; core owns retries and lifecycle transitions.
implementationDecision.rationale: A strict session result removes polling and scheduler coupling from Forge while preserving observable completion evidence.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Replaces distributed polling state with one bounded runtime capability and one strict reducer.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Forge executes an implementation task in a tracked session and only hands off code with verified checks and transcript evidence.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 package delegates session execution to runtime.dispatch and rejects completion without a terminal session, transcript digest, matching attempt identity, changed paths, and passing checks.
implementationDecision.rationale: Session mechanics are generic runtime authority; implementation policy and completion evidence remain package authority.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Keeps the stage as a strict request/result boundary instead of copying the legacy session supervisor.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Blueprint synchronization copies declared control files from the architecture branch, commits changed paths, records state, and reports missing controls for remediation.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 stage preserves the sequence through durable Git, state, and artifact effects and returns a typed remediation result for missing controls.
implementationDecision.rationale: The stage retains domain sequencing while adapters own every privileged mutation.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Removes direct Git and filesystem process orchestration.

parityBlockers: legacy and v2 core behavior are not yet paired at per-surface granularity
observer and notification replacement behavior lacks complete paired delivery/checkpoint tests

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Git workspaces preserve scoped changes, commits, merges, fetch, rebase, push, conflicts, cancellation, and cleanup.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 Git adapter exposes those operations as bounded fenced capabilities with real-Git evidence.
implementationDecision.rationale: All Git mutation belongs in one transactional adapter rather than stage helpers.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Replaces distributed Git helpers with four capability reducers.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Artifacts are atomically persisted, content-addressed, namespaced, size-bounded, and integrity checked.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 artifact store preserves those guarantees behind explicit read/write grants and durable receipts.
implementationDecision.rationale: Artifact persistence is cohesive replaceable authority.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Removes direct artifact filesystem access from every stage.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Trusted code executes bounded subprocesses with exit, signal, output, timeout, cancellation, and cleanup evidence.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The command adapter preserves the process contract with executable and working-root allowlists.
implementationDecision.rationale: The existing adapter is already the smallest safe subprocess boundary.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: One process runner replaces shell helpers across plugins.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Legacy plugins mixed mutable status files and Redis projections.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 state provider offers append-only registration namespaces, monotonic sequence, idempotency, and deterministic replay.
implementationDecision.rationale: Append-only state is simpler and safer than preserving mutable stores.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Deletes mutable projection ownership from plugins.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Legacy integrations performed direct HTTP calls with service-specific policy.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 adapter centralizes bounded origin, method, header, size, timeout, cancellation, and redirect policy.
implementationDecision.rationale: Generic HTTP transport is independent of domain policy.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: One allowlisted adapter replaces repeated request code.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Telemetry could be persisted through mixed local and Redis paths.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The local provider owns append-only evidence while Redis transport is a separate interchangeable provider.
implementationDecision.rationale: Storage transports must not be combined in one adapter.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Separates local durability from network transport.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Legacy integrations read credentials directly from environment and configuration.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The resolver provides allowlisted transient secret values that never enter durable requests, receipts, or events.
implementationDecision.rationale: Secret resolution is a distinct confidential authority.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Removes credential access from all consuming plugins.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Operator messaging mixed transport, authentication, Discord presentation, and notification policy.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 adapter owns only authenticated target-scoped request/response transport; presentation remains observer authority.
implementationDecision.rationale: Transport and presentation have different grants and failure semantics.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Narrows the adapter to confidential delivery and correlation.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Legacy publication was embedded in service-specific integrations.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The HTTP publisher provides target-scoped authenticated idempotent publication without domain policy.
implementationDecision.rationale: HTTP publication is one replaceable provider, not a universal transport.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Consolidates signing, bounds, responses, and cancellation.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Redis transport publishes stream entries with authentication, MAXLEN, idempotency, and durable correlation.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The focused Redis provider atomically deduplicates and appends publication or telemetry entries through authenticated bounded RESP connections.
implementationDecision.rationale: Redis semantics belong in a provider rather than generic HTTP, state, or telemetry packages.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: One small protocol client and Lua transaction replace domain Redis imports.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Agent dispatch owns authenticated session execution, liveness, terminal results, transcripts, cancellation, and confidential correlation.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The runtime provider owns host session mechanics and returns closed terminal session evidence consumed by domain stages.
implementationDecision.rationale: Stages must not receive credentials or raw host session APIs.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Moves reusable session supervision behind one capability.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Durable waits enforce typed signals, authorized issuers, expiry, duplicate and stale rejection, and restart.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The wait adapter preserves storage and validation while core exclusively owns pause, claim, and resume lifecycle.
implementationDecision.rationale: Wait persistence and lifecycle state transitions are separate authorities.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Deletes duplicate watcher and resume paths.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Git workspaces preserve scoped changes, commits, merges, synchronization, conflicts, cancellation, and cleanup.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 Git adapter preserves observable Git results through bounded fenced operations.
implementationDecision.rationale: All Git mutation belongs in one adapter.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Removes Git helpers from stages and core.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Artifacts have one authoritative owner, stable identity, integrity, and bounded visibility.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 artifact store enforces that authority through namespaced capability grants.
implementationDecision.rationale: Artifact ownership remains equivalent while direct access is deleted.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Centralizes validation and persistence.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: One shared module assembled role-specific prose, filesystem paths, shell commands, completion artifacts, and compatibility shims and performed artifact-context writes while building prompts.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: A dependency-only library creates versioned deterministic data envelopes, rejects unsafe or lossy JSON values, enforces size/depth/entry limits, and owns no domain instructions or effects.
implementationDecision.rationale: Shared prompt infrastructure should standardize safe data and response boundaries, while each stage package owns its domain language and completion semantics.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Deletes global role coupling and prompt-time filesystem effects instead of porting the large helper surface.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Forge prompts bind task identity, Git context, completion evidence, and exact output instructions.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: Implementation-agent owns the equivalent domain protocol and terminal session/evidence contract while shared serialization is data-only.
implementationDecision.rationale: Domain prompt behavior remains with the implementation extension instead of a global helper.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Moves policy to one owner and removes compatibility shims.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Buster prompts bind suite instructions, workspace rules, output schema, and completion ordering.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: Test-agent and quality-gate own their equivalent execution and verdict protocols while shared serialization is data-only.
implementationDecision.rationale: Testing policy belongs to the Buster extensions rather than global prompt infrastructure.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Separates execution policy from generic safe serialization.

parityBlockers: v2 registry consumers and legacy scheduler deletion are not implemented

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Review and approval gates produce closed pass, remediation, blocked, and wait outcomes while core owns lifecycle transitions.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 review and approval registrations return the same closed control outcomes through registration-scoped capabilities.
implementationDecision.rationale: Preserve domain decisions while deleting runner-specific lifecycle coupling.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: One strict reducer per registration replaces mixed gate runner control flow.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Review judges supplied evidence, rejects contradictory PASS verdicts, and requests remediation for actionable failures.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 review package strictly decodes the same evidence classes and returns typed pass or request-fix results.
implementationDecision.rationale: Keep review policy package-local and delegate agent transport and lifecycle to runtime.dispatch.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Removes hidden repository and session coupling from the decision stage.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Approval sends an operator request, durably waits for an authorized approve or reject signal, and resumes once.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 stage constructs the message and typed wait while operator messaging, signal persistence, authorization, and resume attempts stay in their owning capabilities and core.
implementationDecision.rationale: The observable approval protocol remains intact without filesystem watchers or transport details in the stage.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Reduces approval to input validation, message/wait construction, and signal reduction.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Case-study generation combined grounded document creation with optional publication and pipeline presentation concerns.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 package generates a strictly sectioned, identity-bound artifact from supplied facts; publication is a separate adapter concern.
implementationDecision.rationale: Generation and external delivery have different authority, failure, and replacement boundaries.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Deletes presentation and deployment side effects from the generator.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Pipeline review synthesizes run-wide evidence into a retrospective report without changing lifecycle truth.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 reporting stage preserves grounded synthesis and required dimensions and can only write its report artifact.
implementationDecision.rationale: Retrospective reporting remains distinct from the actionable review decision stage.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Removes session polling and notification side effects from report generation.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Project summary delegated formatting to a registered generator and mixed persistence, telemetry, and Discord delivery.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 package deterministically reduces validated run metrics and diagnostics into one stable Markdown artifact.
implementationDecision.rationale: A deterministic summary is cheaper, reproducible, and does not require agent judgment or notification authority.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Replaces a multi-service orchestration path with a pure reducer and one artifact effect.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Validators expose stable pass, remediation, block, reason, and finding control semantics to the scheduler.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: Cohesive v2 stages return the same scheduler-observable control semantics through the closed StageResult contract.
implementationDecision.rationale: The mixed validator facade is replaced by independently owned stages while core retains the generic lifecycle reducer.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Removes the cross-validator union and fixed-kind dispatch without changing observable control outcomes.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: The architecture validator combined software-architecture judgment with graph checks, file presence, runtime configuration validation, session spawning, monitoring, retry, and termination.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The stage owns only software-architecture judgment and rich findings; generic graph validity belongs to core, required-file checks belong to deterministic preflight stages, configuration belongs to registry activation, and session lifecycle belongs to runtime.dispatch.
implementationDecision.rationale: Separating generic orchestration and deterministic validation from architecture judgment follows the target ownership model and avoids duplicating core guarantees.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Deletes stage-specific lifecycle and bookkeeping machinery while preserving architecture verdicts and structured findings.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Architecture judgment returned scoped findings and blocked on blocking or error severity while its service also owned generic runtime lifecycle work.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 package validates closed domain-model and integration-boundary findings and delegates all generic session lifecycle to the runtime capability.
implementationDecision.rationale: This keeps domain judgment package-local and moves reusable runtime behavior to its proper privileged adapter.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Reduces the stage to prompt, strict decoding, artifact evidence, and a typed result.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Delivery lint validates Dockerfile/static delivery declarations and returns pass, remediation, or blocked outcomes with stable reports.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The authoritative v2 delivery-lint package retains those outcomes, reason codes, repository reads, and report artifacts.
implementationDecision.rationale: Phase 8 already proved the direct deterministic implementation and deleted the legacy owner.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Keeps one small implementation and no compatibility facade.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Pre-check and full lint discover applicable tools, execute the policy tier, normalize findings, and emit deterministic reports.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 lint package retains the proven data-driven engine behind separate pre-check and full registrations plus a bounded executor adapter.
implementationDecision.rationale: The engine complexity reflects supported tools and policies; rewriting it would add parity risk without reducing the small v2 orchestration boundary.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Removes legacy process orchestration while reusing the mature tool engine and stable fingerprints.

implementationDecision.legacyBehavior: Preflight verifies that owned Dockerfile and API artifacts are declared by Forge blueprints, including split-module blueprints.
implementationDecision.replacementBehavior: The v2 stage performs the same declaration checks through bounded repository reads and emits a closed result and report artifact.
implementationDecision.rationale: The rules remain intact while direct filesystem and logger dependencies are replaced by capabilities.
implementationDecision.complexityImpact: Reduces global configuration coupling and makes substep handling explicit.
